goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — A failure of the retry-count update inside catch escapes the handler and aborts processing the remaining reminders instead of preserving the original best-effort error handling.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that at line 186-193, inside the catch block, there's a new `await prisma.workflowReminder.update()` call that is not wrapped in its own try-catch. If this database update fails, it will throw an exception that propagates up and out of the for loop processing reminders, aborting the processing of remaining reminders. The original code only had `console.log` in the catch block which couldn't fail, preserving the best-effort behavior of continuing to process other reminders even when one fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — If recording a retry fails inside the catch block, that new exception escapes and aborts the cron run before later reminders are processed.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at lines 183-192 in the diff, inside the catch block there's a prisma.workflowReminder.update() call that is not wrapped in its own try-catch. If this database update fails, it will throw an exception that escapes the outer catch block, causing the entire handler to abort before processing remaining reminders in the loop. This is a real defect - the catch block intended to handle errors gracefully but introduces a new failure point.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:39 — The retry cleanup is not limited to SMS reminders, so it deletes any workflow reminder whose retryCount exceeds one regardless of method or scheduled date.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at lines 31-43 that the deleteMany query uses an OR condition where the second condition only checks `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` without any method filter. This means any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 will be deleted, regardless of whether it's an SMS reminder or another type (like email). This is a real bug since the function is specifically for SMS reminders (scheduleSMSReminders.ts) but the cleanup logic affects all reminder types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — Retrying with a read-then-write retryCount value loses increments from overlapping cron runs, allowing repeated failures to evade the retry limit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that retryCount is read from the database at query time (line 56-58), then later incremented using `reminder.retryCount + 1` (lines 184 and 193). If two cron runs overlap and both read the same retryCount value before either writes, they will both write the same incremented value, losing one increment. This is a classic read-modify-write race condition. The deletion logic at line 37 deletes reminders where `retryCount > 1`, so if increments are lost due to race conditions, reminders could fail more than 2 times without being deleted, evading the retry limit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:29 — The new retry lifecycle has no tests for incrementing on a failed schedule and deleting the reminder after the retry limit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new retry logic: incrementing retryCount on failed SMS scheduling (lines 178-186 and 190-197) and deleting reminders where retryCount > 1 (lines 37-41). This is nontrivial business logic that affects data lifecycle. The finding correctly identifies that there are no tests visible in this diff for this new behavior. While we cannot verify from the diff alone whether tests exist elsewhere, the finding is specific and grounded in actual new code that implements retry increment and deletion logic.
